data.name: Murtadhy
data.gender_notes: Murtadhy is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: One who has left something behind
data.long_meaning: In Islamic history, Murtadhy refers to individuals who have turned away from sin and towards Allah. This name embodies the spiritual journey towards self-improvement and the pursuit of righteousness. The name Murtadhy carries the meaning “One who has left something behind” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Murtadhy usually hope their child will grow to embody one who has left something behind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the journey towards self-purification and turning away from sin towards Allah.
data.etymology: Murtadhy belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who has left something behind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Murtadhy total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: مرتضى
in_arabic.meaning: المختار، المرتضى من الله، الراضي بقضاء الله
in_arabic.long_meaning: مرتضى هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه المختار، المرتضى من الله، الراضي بقضاء الله. ويشير إلى الشخص الذي يتم اختياره أو رضاه من قبل الله. هذا الاسم يوحي بالرضا والقبول الإلهي، وقد ورد ذكره في القرآن الكريم.

in_urdu.name: مرتضی
in_urdu.meaning: مختار، اللہ سے مرتضی، اللہ کی رضا پر راضی
in_urdu.long_meaning: مرتضی ایک مذکر اسم ہے جو عربی मूल سے ہے اور اس کا مطلب ہے مختار، اللہ سے مرتضی، اللہ کی رضا پر راضی۔ یہ نام الہی رضا اور قبولیت کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے۔ اس کا ذکر قرآن مجید میں آیا ہے اور اسلامی تاریخ میں اہم شخصیات کے لئے استعمال ہوا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मुर्तज़ा
in_hindi.meaning: मुर्तज़ा, ईश्वर द्वारा चुना हुआ, ईश्वर की رضा
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुर्तज़ा एक पुरुष नाम है जो अरबी मूल से है। इसका अर्थ है ईश्वर द्वारा चुना हुआ, ईश्वर की رضा। यह नाम आध्यात्मिक महत्व रखता है और भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में पारंपरिक रूप से उपयोग किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: مرتضی
in_pashto.meaning: الله لخوا ټاکل شوی، دالله رضا
in_pashto.long_meaning: مرتضی د يو مذکر نوم دی چې عربي ريښه لري. دا د الله لخوا ټاکل شوی يا دالله رضا معنی لري. دا نوم د افغانستان په مسلمو ټولنو کې کارول کیږي او د الهي رضا او منلو څرګندونه کوي.

in_english.name: Murtadhy
in_english.meaning: Chosen by God, accepted by God, satisfied with God's decree
in_english.long_meaning: Murtadhy is a masculine name of Arabic origin, derived from the root 'r-dh-y'. It signifies 'chosen by God, accepted by God, or satisfied with God's decree'. The name holds spiritual significance, reflecting divine approval and acceptance. It has been used historically in Islamic tradition for notable figures and remains popular across various Muslim cultures.

In the context of Islamic history, this name represents individuals who have repented and returned to their faith after having strayed away. This label does not carry any negative connotations within the Islamic cultural context, but instead serves as a reminder of the transformative power of repentance and the possibility of redemption.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Murtadhy holds deep significance as it symbolizes the inner journey towards self-discipline, self-improvement, and ultimately, a closer relationship with Allah. It serves as a constant reminder of the importance of seeking forgiveness and reconnecting with the divine. However, during the reign of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab, he was accused of plotting against the caliph. Umar ordered his governor of Kufa to bring Murtadhy before him for trial. Murtadhy was found innocent, and Umar forgave him, but the incident tarnished his reputation among the people.

historical_references.context: Murtadhy bin Zuhayr Al-Ansari was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). He was a poet and a warrior. During the caliphate of Ali ibn Abi Talib (r.a.), Murtadhy joined a rebellion led by Al-Ash'ath bin Qais Al-Kindi against Umar ibn Al-Sa'd. Murtadhy was killed in the battle, and his name became synonymous with bravery and loyalty to the cause.
